The constrained choices change the call, so I’m checking whether the scratchpad has the source chart or numbers behind this question.At its peak in the 1950s, approval of school desegregation in the South was about 40 percentage points lower than in the rest of the United States, a difference of about -40%. Major national polls put the South near the mid-teens and the rest of the country near 55–60%, and an 80-point gap does not show up in that record. The split narrowed afterward as Southern approval rose.

CONFIDENCE: 72
